P5-wasm-002 does not pass. The gate fails as committed: aegis-p2 still doesn't call the new code, the cordon path doesn't exist yet, and the oracle has a defect. No check was weakened. The supplied patches are verified locally (not committed): with them the gate passes 68/68 and the self-test is clean.

**Built inside write scope** (crates/aegis-wasm/src/abi/**, crates/aegis-wasm/tests/abi.rs):
- mod.rs: the static import/export check. Any non-F14 import (env.host_fault in a golden build, WASI, unknown aegis names, wrong types, memory/global/table imports) and any wrong export set is refused before instantiation. F14Worker::new repeats the check. The old define_imports stub is kept for the import-free store::Worker.
- frame.rs: F14 frame codec. Decoders are total and strict.
- headers.rs: the I5 response-header rules.
- host.rs: the eight host functions. Handles are generation-tagged per request (forged, foreign, stale or zero traps 5). Five quotas are enforced (host calls, data_run count, data bytes, response bytes, log bytes; traps 6) before anything over a quota is forwarded. ABI misuse traps 7. Large writes are chunked to fit the frame cap. data_run blocks on the matching data-reply. test-hooks builds get env.host_fault.
- serve.rs: F14Worker and Session. Each request gets a fresh Store with fuel and the epoch deadline armed before instantiation and a limiter at the request's memory cap; limits are min(frame values, boot ceilings). A new generation is drawn per request. A cancel drops the request; out-of-order frames end the session without a reply.
- mutant.rs: the five worker mutants, selected by AEGIS_P2_MUTANT in mutants builds only; golden builds compile them out.
- fi.rs is untouched; p2-subject still builds clean.

**Gate numbers** (laptop, Linux 6.17.0-14):

Mutants builds send the D8 layout frame, which hostile.py rejects as "frame for unknown req-id", so every zygote mutant cell is red for that reason (100 of 112 red cells). The cordon cells are red on exactly the expected case for each mutant.

open_issues: Scope block, integrator: crates/aegis-p2/src/zygote.rs (P5-iso-002 scope; that unit is closed) must switch to aegis_wasm::abi::F14Worker/Session. Patch: crates/aegis-wasm/src/abi/patches/aegis-p2-zygote.patch (applies on f29d17f). It also adds the binary-side mutant hooks: no-fuel-no-epoch drops ITIMER_REAL; no-limiter sizes the pool at MEMORY_MIB_MAX, because otherwise the pool at memory_mib masks a missing limiter.

P5-iso-003: the gate needs a cordon. Minimal wiring: after the sandbox install, start EpochTicker (the install refuses a multi-threaded process), send frame::ready(digest), then call worker.session(conn).serve_all(). patches/aegis-p2-cordon-sketch.patch is a verification sketch only (no registry, crash budget or idle reaping) and depends on the zygote patch.

Oracle defect (oracles/, integrator): hostile.py exchange() rejects the D8 layout frame that mutants builds send, so the worker self-test is vacuous on the zygote path. Fix: patches/hostile-modules-layout.patch (accepts one layout frame before any other frame of an exchange).

Session serves one request at a time. F14 allows multiplexed req-ids on a cordon connection; a frame for another req-id during a request ends the session. P5-iso-003 and P5-bin-001 must not pipeline requests on one cordon connection, or the session needs extending.

The worker is not told the configured limits.max_header_fields / max_header_list_size, so it bounds them by the F8 maxima (256 / 65536) and leaves the configured values to the supervisor's re-check. frame_max defaults to 64 KiB (F14Worker::with_frame_max exists, but there is no CLI flag yet).
MAX_REQ_BODY is 64 MiB, while F8 max_body_bytes allows up to 1 GiB. P2 routes need a supervisor-side body cap at or below 64 MiB (P5-bin-001); a larger body currently ends the worker session.
The test-hooks env.host_fault(2) corruption flag on the F14 path (abi::host_corrupted) is separate from fi::host_corrupted. No oracle exercises it on the F14 path yet.

result.summary:
The unit is not passing yet, but only because of write scope. Everything in the acceptance is green on the committed tree except the MPK run of p2-fault-cordon. That run needs two patches to files outside my scope. They are in subjects/p2-subject/patches/ and the case is written up in subjects/p2-subject/INFEASIBLE_REPORT.md. With both applied, the MPK run passes. No check or threshold was weakened.

**What I built**
- **aegis-iso cordon table:** `cordon::Registry<K, C>` is the supervisor's cordon table, keyed by principal.
  - Any id-based get, release or remove by a principal other than the owner is refused (ForeignPrincipal).
  - The table is bounded by max_cordons. At the cap it evicts the least-recently-used idle cordon. With none idle it refuses (AtCapacity, 503) and never shares a cordon.
  - Idle cordons are reaped after cordon_idle_s.
- **aegis-iso serve loop:** `cordon::serve` runs after Profile::cordon is installed in the single-threaded process.
  - It starts serving threads on demand, up to --threads.
  - I found that 64 threads waiting in accept for 16 clients on one pinned core stalled running requests for over 100 ms. The 100 ms epoch deadline then trapped healthy requests. Starting threads on demand removed those failures.
- **aegis-iso crash budget:** `crash_budget::CrashBudget<K>` is pure logic over instants the caller supplies.
  - 3 crashes within 60 s give 429 for 600 s, counted from the third crash.
  - It is kept per principal, and healthy failures never count.
- **aegis-p2 cordon:** `aegis-p2 cordon --module --sha256 [--mpk --memory-mib --pool-slots --threads]`.
  - Boot: digest-checked load, then Profile::cordon, then the epoch ticker and the serve loop.
  - Protocol: it sends the F14 ready frame, plus the layout frame in test-hooks and mutants builds. Requests on one connection run in order; connections run in parallel.
  - Outcomes: a cancel drops the request, and a wall timeout comes back as resp-end trap 2.
  - Checked locally and on the desktop with `tools/cordon_smoke.py`: digest correct, resp-end answers, fuel trap and wall trap both returned, cordon stays alive.
- **p2-subject:** `serve cordon [--threads N] [--mpk]`, with the mutants shared-store, recycle50, no-deadline and epoch-only-4.

**D17 decision:** on the forkwasm path, a fork child killed by SIGALRM stays a worker death. That maps to the Deny response and is charged as an abnormal exit. The supervisor needs nothing more.

| isolation-fi `--trials 3 --path cordon`, no MPK | PASS. 0 healthy failures and 0 wrong answers on all six gated classes. oom recovery p99 3520 µs, loop throughput ×0.68 | 7.4–7.9 |
| hostabort / hostpoison (reported, not gated) | 2.82 failures per fault / 99.5 wrong answers per fault | same run |
| `--mpk`, committed tree | FAIL: server not ready (the cordon dies by SIGSYS) | 6.9 |

open_issues: The MPK run fails on the committed tree. Wasmtime 50.0.1 with MPK calls pkey_mprotect (nr 329) on every instance allocation, and the cordon seccomp filter kills it. Fix: subjects/p2-subject/patches/P5-iso-003-filter-pkey_mprotect.patch, which adds it to the ALLOWLIST in crates/aegis-iso/src/sandbox/filter.rs (P5-iso-001's file; pkey_alloc stays denied after install).

With that fixed, MPK splits the 64-slot pool into 16 stripes of 4 slots, and a full stripe refuses healthy requests ('maximum concurrent limit of 4 for memory stripe N reached'). Fix: subjects/p2-subject/patches/P5-iso-003-aegis-wasm-mpk-stripe-retry.patch, which retries with a new Store (next stripe) only when MPK is on. It touches engine/mod.rs and store/mod.rs (P5-wasm-001, done) and fi.rs, which the parallel P5-wasm-002 owns under D20. I reported fi.rs and did not edit it, so apply the patch in coordination with P5-wasm-002. The aegis-wasm tests (10/10) and clippy pass with it.

crates/aegis-p2/src/cordon.rs carries its own copy of the F14 frame codec, because zygote.rs keeps its codec private and is outside my scope. Whoever wires req-head, data-run and data-reply into zygote.rs must make the same change in cordon.rs, or move the codec into one shared module.

The aegis-p2 cordon handles one request at a time per connection (F14 allows up to cordon_slots in flight) and runs connections in parallel. Multiplexing several requests on one connection is not implemented.
Observed in aegis-wasm, not my code: when a request ends on the wall-bound trap, resp-end reports fuel-used 0. It is an untrusted accounting value, but the number looks wrong.

Not verified here: aegis-bin integration of the cordon table, crash budget and respawn (P5-bin-001), and p2-e2e or hostile-modules runs against the aegis-p2 cordon. Laptop timing numbers are provisional (grade at most B).
